description: High availability for the module's guest: which node it fails over to, and how often its disk is replicated there.
_note: cluster:ha is a drift reconciler, but NOT a per-field one, and the difference matters. Most of what it repairs has no module field behind it at all — the HA resource being absent or not 'started', the node-affinity rule missing, the replication job missing, the guest sitting on the wrong node — because those follow from DECLARING cluster:ha, not from any field's value. The drift record is keyed by field, so those units cannot be expressed in it. Its state also spans three Proxmox subsystems (/cluster/ha/resources, /cluster/ha/rules, /cluster/replication) that must be reconciled together: re-pointing HANode changes the affinity rule AND recreates the replication job, one decision across two planes. So the existing loop stays and both fields are apply:'reconcile'; what the manifest adds is the declared cost of changing them.

HANode.note: The failover node. Changing it re-points the node-affinity rule and recreates the ZFS replication job against the new target — which means a full initial re-sync, so it is IO-heavy and can take a long time. It is still in-place: the running guest is not moved, not rebooted, and stays served throughout. The move that DOES relocate a guest is cluster:vm's `node`, which defers to this service for an HA module.

replicationSchedule.note: How often the guest's disk is replicated to the failover node — the bound on how much is lost if the primary dies. A `pvesr update`: it changes when the next run happens, nothing else.
